transcript: The Encores Series at City Center can be hit or miss, and Love Life is unfortunately the latter for me. This 1948 musical is a commentary on American life and love, told through a series of scenes from the never ending lives of one married couple, alternating with some vaudeville-esque performances. In this production, the couple is portrayed by Brian Stokes Mitchell and Kate Baldwin as their relationship and the world around them changes. It's rare for me to find the book of a musical to be the most interesting component, but this one caught my attention because for an older musical, it feels ahead of its time. In the context of 2025, I interpret it as a commentary on how capitalism and chasing the American dream is arguably and ironically the biggest antithesis to life, liberty, and the pursuit of happiness. But even though I found the concepts and themes interesting, I found the show itself pretty boring. The score, though pleasant and full of lush orchestrations which are beautifully performed here, is lacking sonic variation. With most of the songs being too long and very one-note, the show was a bit of slog. Which is a bummer because I really wanted to appreciate this production and its expectedly lovely vocal performance from Brian Stokes Mitchell, but let's just say it didn't make me question why the show is seldom produced. With that, another program for my collection.
